# Elite Redux Wiki (in-game)

# How to work on this document

This document helps us to define what we want to show in our new in-game wiki. Anyone with the link to this document can edit.

# Wiki Structure

**Category 1** (e.g. Basic Information)  
\--- Entry 1 (e.g. Talk to Nurse Joy)  
\------ Page 1 of Entry 1 (e.g. Talk to Nurse Joy in any Pokémon Center to receive lots of items)  
\--- Entry 2 (e.g. Pokémon Changes)  
\------ Page 1 of Entry 2 (e.g. Almost every Pokémon has been improved for better balance and utility)

**Technical limitations**

* We can have up to 5 pages of each entry (which is a lot)  
* Per each info page, we should not exceed 9 lines of text

# Actual Wiki Content

This is the content which will be shown in-game.

## Basic Information

### 	Talk to Nurse Joy

* Talk to Nurse Joy in any Pokémon Center to receive a DexNav+, Infinite Repel, Battle Items, all Pokéballs, all Berries, all Type Gems, etc.  
* Each time you speak to her, all items get refilled.  
* Mega Stones are the only items not given by Nurse Joy.

### Online Pokédex

* [https://dex.elite-redux.com](https://dex.elite-redux.com)  
* The Online Dex shows all information about Pokémon, Abilities, Moves, Locations and Trainers.  
* You can also build teams there, for theorycrafting.

### Pokémon Changes

* Almost every Pokémon has been improved for better balance and utility.  
* Notable reworks:  
* **Kecleon**: Colour Change now activates before an attack hits and changes Kecleon's type to the most favourable matchup, which functionally makes it immune to every attack with a type-based immunity and resistant to all other attacks.  
* **Eeveelutions**: All of the Eeveelutions can now devolve back into Eevee, preserving their movepools. This means that all eight essentially share their movepools and, thus, have unparalleled type coverage in addition to varied STAB moves.  
* **Hatterene**: In addition to innate Pixilate and Magic Bounce, it has innate Hyper Aggressive (a Parental Bond clone), and its ability Twisted Dimensions sets Trick Room for three turns on entry.  
* **Dewgong**: Ability choices are Fur Coat, Ice Scales, and Arctic Fur, which is a lesser version of both combined. It also has innate North Wind to let it auto-set Aurora Veil for three turns on entry.  
* **Gliscor**: In addition to having Poison Heal, it gets Rough Skin to improve its physical defensive utility, and also Tectonize as an ability to turn Facade into a Ground-type move.  
* **Pyukumuku**: Now has 600 BST, innate Unaware, and Pressure (which has been buffed to cast Haze on entry as well as its vanilla function).  
* **Braviary**: Now stacks Defiant, Flock (Flying-type Overgrow), buffed Big Pecks, and possible Sheer Force or Gale Wings to give it immense attacking power.  
* **Phione**: With innate High Tide, it uses Surf at 50BP after using any Water move. It also has Field Explorer to empower 'field' moves (e.g. Headbutt, Surf), and Soul-Heart as an ability option.  
* **Exploud**: \[now a pseudo, also Loud Bang\]  
* **Dodrio**: \[idk someone suggested it, honestly i think Fearow fits more\]  
* **Aurorus**: \[resists most of its weaknesses, defensive colossus\]  
* Check the Online Pokédex for details.

  ### Move Changes

* Many moves have been improved, especially in terms of accuracy and power.  
* OHKO moves (e.g. Fissure) now deal approximately 120 damage with 80% accuracy.  
* Some moves have been given all-new effects, and others have had their functionality completely reworked. Most moves have at least a usable niche.  
* Further details available in the Online Pokédex.

  ### Quality of Life Improvements

* **Portable PC**: Accessible from the Start Menu (disabled for Elite Four).  
* No need to teach HMs; you can fly to any previously visited location with any Pokémon, and other HMs will be unlocked as you complete Gyms.  
* You can register multiple items for easy access using L.

  ### Battle Changes

* All Pokémon now have 31 IVs by default. Use Iron Pill to set Speed to 0 if needed (and back to 31, too).  
* Ace and Elite Mode include Sleep Clause (only one enemy Pokémon can be put to sleep).  
* All moves have PP Max, and held items are regenerated after battles. Your Pokemon also heal to full automatically after most battles. There are some battles designed to be a gauntlet \- without healing in between.

  ### Battle UI Changes

* Press L during battles to bring up this in-game wiki. This shortcut can be changed in Settings \> Custom (press R).  
* Now you also see a move's effectiveness before attacking. This even considers abilities and innates like Levitate or Sap Sipper\!  
* STAB (50% Same Type Attack Bonus) is indicated with a \+ icon.  
* Trainer battles can now be forfeited, sending you back to the last Pokémon Center. This will count as a loss in the statistics.

  ### Acquiring Pokémon

* You will receive one of each Pokéball from Nurse Joy, all with a 100% catch rate. You don’t lose the Pokéballs if you use them.  
* The upgraded DexNav+ now allows you to search for any Pokemon in an area automatically. You can also spend BP to acquire Pokemon directly without battling.  
* Shiny rates can be boosted up to 1/5 in the Options menu.  
* Every Pokémon from Generations 1 to 9 is available.  
* You can purchase Redux Pokemon for BP in the Adoption Center. More species will be unlocked as you progress in your journey.

  ### Switching Nature

* Switch a Pokémon’s nature directly in the Summary Screen.  
* Natures increase one base stat by 10% while decreasing another by 10%.  
* These will be indicated by arrows pointing up and down on the summary screen next to the affected stats.

  ### Changing Hidden/Secret Power

* Use Type Gems (provided by Nurse Joy) to modify a Pokémon’s Hidden Power and Secret Power (physical version) types.

  ### Setting EVs

* Directly assign EVs in the Summary Screen — no grinding required.  
* Each stat can have up to 252 EVs, with a total limit of 510 EVs.  
* Typically, you will get the best results by distributing 252 EVs across your two best stats.  
* Investing in HP tends to be more useful than investing in one defense, unless your Pokemon has very high base HP and much lower defenses.

  ### Learning Moves

* Learn new moves easily in the Party or Move menu (press R).  
* Certain moves still require leveling up. These moves are found in the Level list, while the other lists show moves available to a Pokemon by move category.  
* Typically, you will unlock at least a few moves on each Pokemon after each gym in Elite caps, up until around 2/3s of the game. Some Pokemon will learn all their moves faster or slower.

  ### Evolutions

* All Pokemon with unusual evolution methods are now just level-based evolutions. You can see whether a Pokemon can still evolve, and what level it will happen at, on the Summary screen.  
* Potential Mega Evolutions are shown on the Summary screen too, even if you don't have the correct Mega Stone, but you cannot use them without it.  
* You can choose to evolve a Pokemon from the Party menu, and select which evolution to get if it has branched evolutions.  
* Leveling up can also be done from the Party menu. Level Caps and scaling enemies will ensure you don't overlevel by accident.

## Ability Information

### 	Innates

* Pokemon can have one to three abilities, which you can change freely from the summary menu. Most Pokemon have three choices. You can also see these abilities in more detail by selecting them from the summary.  
* In addition, Pokemon have three 'innates', which are tied to their species. All three of a Pokemon's innates are always active in addition to its ability.  
* On higher difficulties, most innates start off locked. Defeat Gym Leaders and raise the level cap to unlock them.

### 	New Abilities

* Elite Redux has 500+ new abilities. Some of these are designed for specific mons to make them more powerful/interesting, some are combination abilities, and some are new generic abilities given to many Pokemon.  
* Some examples include Chloroplast, which makes the user's moves function as if the weather is Sun regardless of the actual weather; Phantom Pain, which causes Ghost-type moves to affect Normal-types; Fungal Infection, which causes the user's contact moves to inflict Leech Seed; and Fort Knox, which blocks abilities that would increase the power of an enemy's offensive moves.

### 	Changed Abilities

* Many existing abilities have been revised to make them more powerful and give them a niche.  
* These include Stall, which now reduces incoming damage by 30% if your Pokemon hasn't moved this turn; Battle Armour and Shell Armour, which reduce all damage by 20% in addition to blocking critical hits; Big Pecks, which is now a Tough Claws clone; Storm Drain and Lightning Rod, which now boost the user's higher offensive stat on activation; and Frisk, which now disables the enemy's item for two turns after checking it.

## Battle Information

### General Information about Status Effects

* Elite Redux changes the way a few effects work, such as Confusion and Infatuation, while also introducing new ones; notably, Bleed, Fear and Frostbite (semi-new, replaces Freeze).

### Burn, Paralysis, Poison, Sleep

* These statuses remain unchanged in Elite Redux.  
* Burn deals 1/8 of the burned Pokémon's health and halves damage done by physical attacks.  
* Paralysis reduces the Speed stat of the Pokémon and has a 25% chance of rendering it unable to move during its turn.  
* Poison deals 1/8 damage of the Pokémon's health over time, and if Badly Poisoned, it starts at 1/16 each turn and increases by 1/16 on each following turn.  
* Sleep makes a Pokémon unable to move during its turn.

### New Status Effects

* Bleed

    
  Bleed is a unique, non-volatile status effect that Elite Redux introduces. Whereas other status conditions are usually associated with a type, Bleed is mainly associated with Keen Edge boosted moves, but are not exclusive to that category.


  Bleed deals 1/16th of the Pokémon's health as damage, similar to other damaging statuses. However, bleed also prevents healing effects, as well as negates stat boosts. Rock and Ghost Type Pokémon are immune to this status effect.

    
  Using healing moves will cure the effect, but will not heal the Pokémon that turn.

* Fear

  Fear is a new status condition that traps the target for 2 turns. During this time, the inflicted Pokémon will take an increased 50% damage.

  Moves that inflict Fear:  
  Scary Face, Terror Charge, Worry Seed  
* Frostbite (semi-new, replaces Freeze)

  Still does 1/16 HP damage of the affected Pokémon every turn to non-Ice-types like Hail.

  Also halves damage done by special attacks.

### Changed Status Effects

* Confusion

  Removing the RNG elements of Confusion, it now simply has the confused Pokémon take 33% of the damage it deals as recoil.  
* Infatuation

  Infatuation has been reworked in Elite Redux. Infatuated targets now deal 50% less damage from both physical and special moves.

### General Weather Information

* Weather effects from moves and abilities last 8 turns (12 turns with Weather Rocks).  
* Hail/Snow

  Boosts Ice-types’ Defense by 50%.  
  Damages non-Ice types (1/16 HP per turn).

  Blizzard ignores accuracy checks.

* Sandstorm

  Damages non-Rock, Ground, or Steel types (1/16 HP per turn).

  Boosts Rock-types’ Sp. Def by 50%.

* Rain

  Boosts Water-type moves by 50%.

  Weakens Fire-type moves by 50%.

  Thunder and Hurricane ignore accuracy checks.

* Sunlight

  Boosts Fire-type moves by 50%.

  Weakens Water-type moves by 50%.

  Prevents freezing.

  Solar Beam/Solar Blade become one-turn moves.

  Growth raises Attack and Sp. Atk by two stages.

* Harsh Sunlight

  Boosts Fire-type moves, nullifies Water-type moves.


* Heavy Rain

  Boosts Water-type moves, nullifies Fire-type moves.


* Strong Winds

  Reduces super-effective damage against Flying types to neutral.

### New Weather: Fog

* Elite Redux reintroduces Fog as its its own unique weather, Eerie fog, and induces these additional effects:


- Drains every positive stat boost(s) of non-Ghost/Psychic-type Pokémon by 1 stage at the end of each turn  
- Halves the effect of weather based recovery (eg. Synthesis, Moonlight, Morning Sun)  
- 20% damage reduction to Ghost-type and Psychic-type Pokémon  
- Revival Blessing fails  
- Harvest fails  
- Makes all instances of Curse turn into Ghost-type Curse  
- The move Weather Ball changes to Ghost-type and doubles in power  
- Castform (Foggy) form  
- Some moves like Ominous Wind also double in power

* Smoke Ball (held item) increases the duration of fog from 8 to 12 turns

## Miscellaneous Information

### Permanent Mega Mode

* Permanent Mega Mode is precisely what it sounds like.


* Once you unlock Mega Evolution after talking to Norman, you now have the option to change your Pokémon into their Mega forms outside of battle from the party menu, just like a normal form change.


* This still requires the right Mega Stone to be in your inventory, so no easy Mega Dewgong for you\!


* A Pokémon that has Mega Evolved in this way will not revert back to normal at the end of a battle.


* Because of this, you can have multiple Megas on your team at once, and they can even hold other items\!   
* You can still Mega Evolve Pokémon in the normal way if you like, though.

  ### Where to get the other starters?

* After getting your first starter, you can get a second (random) one after defeating Calvin at Route 102, in the same exact route.  
* After that, other starters are available around Hoenn, after beating Flannery:  
* \- There is a shop in Lavaridge with the Fire types  
* \- The Flower Shop outside of Petalburg Woods has the Grass types  
* The Open-Air Market in Slateport has the Water types  
* Note: If you are far in the game, you can get them all from the Lilycove Department Store.
